record.paper_title: Answering open questions in biology using spatial genomics and structured methods
record.context_brief: Intrinsic vs extrinsic clone size control
record.original_question: Are clonal population sizes controlled mainly by cell-intrinsic properties of the clone itself or by cell-extrinsic features of the surrounding environment, and at what generations or local conditions does clonal expansion slow or stop?

evidence.quote: Although current analyses can identify clonal population sizes, it remains an open question whether these sizes are governed by cell-intrinsic or cell-extrinsic factors. If a set of cells Y represent a connected component of Q, we can identify generations at which clonal expansion slowed or halted, and ask whether clonal size (the cardinality of Y, |Y|) is a function of expression in surrounding cells.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a tissue be modeled as a finite set of cells $C$ together with a spatial adjacency graph $G=(C,E)$ and a gene-expression map $x:C\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$. Suppose each cell carries a heritable lineage barcode that partitions $C$ into clones, and that a lineage tree $T$ is reconstructed so that every internal node corresponds to a generation (division event). For a clone $Y\subseteq C$ that forms a connected component of a subgraph $Q\subseteq G$, let $|Y|$ denote its cardinality (clonal size) and let $g(Y)$ denote the set of generations at which the rate of expansion of $Y$ along $T$ falls below a fixed threshold (i.e.\ slows or halts).

Address the following:

(a) Determine whether $|Y|$ is governed predominantly by cell-intrinsic features of $Y$ (functions of $\{x(c):c\in Y\}$ and the internal structure of the lineage subtree restricted to $Y$) or by cell-extrinsic features of the spatial neighborhood $N(Y)=\{c\in C\setminus Y: \exists\, y\in Y,\,(y,c)\in E\}$ (functions of $\{x(c):c\in N(Y)\}$). Concretely, exhibit a predictor $f$ minimizing expected squared error in estimating $|Y|$, and decide whether the minimizer depends nontrivially on the extrinsic variables.

(b) Characterize the generations $g(Y)$ at which expansion slows or halts, and determine whether $|Y|$ can be written as a measurable function of the expression profile of the surrounding cells $N(Y)$ at those generations.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a biological open problem about whether clonal population sizes in tissues are determined by intrinsic versus extrinsic factors. It is widely recognized as open in the spatial-genomics and lineage-tracing literature, with no definitive resolution; current methods can measure clone sizes but cannot yet conclusively attribute them to intrinsic or extrinsic causes.

status_evidence.title: Answering open questions in biology using spatial genomics and structured methods
status_evidence.snippet: It remains an open question whether clonal population sizes are governed by cell-intrinsic or cell-extrinsic factors.
status_evidence.claim: The intrinsic-vs-extrinsic control of clonal size is described as an open question.
